You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testEncoder()` fails because it expects the `encode()` method of the `Base64` instance encoder to produce base64-encoded output without any extra line breaks or trailing CRLF sequences. Specifically, the test verifies that encoding a given byte array produces exactly the corresponding UTF-8 encoded string byte array.

The current bug report indicates that the instance method `new Base64().encode()` chunks its output into lines of 76 characters and appends a CRLF line separator after each chunk (consistent with MIME rules), which was not the behavior in Commons-Codec 1.3. The static method `Base64.encodeBase64()` didn't change between 1.3 and 1.4 and does not chunk output, so the problem is isolated to the instance method.

Inspection of the `Base64.encode(byte[])` method confirms that it calculates output length and prepares a buffer that includes space for line separators (CRLF) if `lineLength` is set. The method `getEncodeLength` computes the buffer length by adding the length of chunk separators multiple times based on the chunk size (likely 76 by default).

The `encode(byte[], int, int)` method contains the core logic. When encoding the last bytes (inAvail < 0), if `lineLength` > 0 and `pos > 0`, it appends `lineSeparator` to the output buffer at line 485-486. Also, during encoding in the `else` block, if the current output line reaches `lineLength`, it inserts the lineSeparator bytes (line 506-507). This means the encoded output will be broken into chunks separated by line separators.

Therefore, the root cause is that by default, the instance `Base64` encoder uses chunking with a 76-character line length and appends CRLF line separators. The failing test expects unchunked output without extra line separators. This change in default behavior is why the test fails with the new version.

No relevant information from recent bug reports is seen; they are about different encoding schemes.

Summary:
- Test fails because `Base64().encode()` adds CRLF line separators every 76 characters.
- The instance encoder defaults to chunked output with line separators.
- The test expects a single continuous base64 string without CRLF.
- Prior behavior (Commons-Codec 1.3) did not chunk output, so test breaks with new default.

This is a design or default-configuration issue with the instance encoder's lineLength and lineSeparator fields causing the test failure.

The proper fix would be either to:
- Change the test to expect chunked output with CRLF in output.
- Or configure the `Base64` instance in the test with `lineLength=0` (no chunking) so output matches the test expectations.

Methods to inspect for fixes would be the constructor or initialization methods of `Base64` that set the default `lineLength` and `lineSeparator`, as well as the `encode()` instance method itself.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
